answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a stake locked in a public contract and require that stake to be slashed when the identity signs conflicting claims. If voting weight is capped per identity, an attacker cannot gain influence by registering thousands of names; each name needs its own funded bond, and detected equivocation destroys those funds. A summit proposal can pass through a prism of independent attestations before settlement, while basalt describes the bond’s immovable cost: capital stays locked and risks forfeiture for every fabricated identity.
